idiom_name: abc.ABC with no abstract members plus ABCMeta.register
implementation_notes: Python's closest equivalent is an abstract base class with no abstract members: subclass it, or register unrelated classes with ABCMeta.register, and test with isinstance/issubclass; the numbers tower (numbers.Number) is the stdlib precedent for a data-free ABC used as a category. Registration is the escape hatch for classes you cannot modify, but it enforces nothing and does not appear in the MRO, and plain duck typing is often the more Pythonic choice. Prefer an ABC when the category must be visible to isinstance and to static checkers; prefer a Protocol for structural typing.
code_sketch:
from abc import ABC

class Deletable(ABC):      # marker: no methods
    pass

Deletable.register(str)     # virtual subclass, no inheritance needed
isinstance("x", Deletable)  # True
pitfalls: Virtual subclasses skip all checks; registration only declares a relationship and never enforces methods.
ABCs constrain metaclasses, so combining ABC markers with other ABC hierarchies can raise metaclass conflicts.
A marker ABC does not stop duck-typed cooperation: code that never checks isinstance sees no effect at all.

variants.name: runtime_checkable Protocol
variants.implementation_notes: Structural protocols describe the members a type must have, and @runtime_checkable enables isinstance/issubclass checks that test attribute presence. An empty protocol is the degenerate marker case - and a trap, because checking zero attributes is trivially satisfied, so an empty runtime-checkable Protocol matches every object; the typing documentation notes runtime checks are not completely safe and never verify signatures. Use protocols for static duck typing, and give the protocol a real (even minimal) member when you need it as a runtime marker.
pitfalls: An empty runtime-checkable protocol matches everything - use a sentinel attribute or an explicit registry instead of relying on emptiness.
Runtime protocol checks verify attribute presence only; signatures, types and semantics are never checked.
Protocols cannot be instantiated and do not appear in the MRO, so protocol membership and class inheritance do not mix freely.
